answer_text:
# AltaVista: The Rise and Fall of a Search Pioneer 🔍

## What Was AltaVista?

AltaVista (a contraction of *alta* + *vista*, meaning **"high view"** in Spanish), based in Palo Alto, California, was a web search engine. It was created by researchers at **Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC)** who were trying to showcase the company's hardware to make it easier to find files on the company's public network.

---

## Launch & Early Success

On **December 15, 1995**, less than six months after the start of the project, AltaVista opened to the public with an index of 16 million documents. It was an immediate success, with more than 300,000 searchers using the engine on its first day.

It was the first **"full text" / boolean searchable index** of the World Wide Web. AltaVista was also the first search engine to allow **natural language queries** on the World Wide Web.

At launch, AltaVista had two key innovations: it used a fast, multi-threaded web crawler called **Scooter** that could cover many more web pages than were believed to exist at the time, and it had an efficient backend database, **TurboVista**, running on advanced hardware.

Web traffic increased steadily from 300,000 hits on the first day to more than **80 million hits per day** by 1997, making it one of the most popular websites at the time.

---

## Key Milestones & Innovations

- In 1996, AltaVista became the **exclusive provider of search results for Yahoo**.
- In 1997, it launched **Babel Fish**, a web-based machine translation application that translated text or webpages.
- AltaVista is also credited with implementing the **first CAPTCHA** to prevent fraudulent account registrations and bots from automatically adding pages to its web index.
- Other innovations include the **first multilingual search** capacity on the Internet and the first search technology to support Chinese, Japanese, and Korean languages.

---

## Ownership Changes & Decline

In January 1998, **Compaq acquired DEC** for $9.6 billion, and as part of the transaction, Compaq acquired AltaVista.

In January 1999, Compaq spun off AltaVista and began a redesign of the site as a **web portal** to compete with Yahoo. This proved to be a critical strategic mistake. AltaVista did not fail as a search engine itself — the service failed when it tried to become the next Yahoo or MSN.

Traffic plummeted shortly thereafter due to **competition from Google Search** and others.

In February 2003, **Overture Services** acquired AltaVista for $140 million. In July 2003, **Yahoo acquired Overture** for $1.63 billion.

---

## Shutdown

Yahoo purchased AltaVista in 2003 (when purchasing Overture Services) and **shut altavista.com down on July 8, 2013**. In June 2013, the domain name was redirected to **Yahoo Search**.

---

## Legacy

AltaVista remains a landmark in internet history. It created what would later become known as the **first ever modern search engine**, inspiring a period of online search that remains largely unchanged over two decades on. Nevertheless, AltaVista will always be part of the Internet's history, as other early search engines such as Archie.
